messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high-severity: serving-runtime model-load-failure on cluster-us-west-2. Alert rate: 30/m. Affected service: redwood-serving-runtime-prod. Pager routed to #incidents and @alice (oncall)  

alice (oncall): seen. starting triage — checking recent deploys and autoscale events.

alice (oncall): logs show repeated container restarts on node gpu-12; crash loop with CUDA OOM during model load: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/loader.py", line 198, in load_model
    state_dict = torch.load(f, map_location=device)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 27.50 GiB already allocated)
```

alice (oncall): also saw lines like `RuntimeError: Failed to deserialize tensor` and occasional `compile timeout: 120.0s exceeded` when the JIT kernel compile runs.

ben (sre): I'm joining. can you paste the pod logs + kube events? I want to check node flaps and OOMKill counts.

alice (oncall): pasted kube events and pod logs. quick summary: scale-up triggered 3 new pods trying to load model-10-big. two of three fail during load; host gpu-12 shows GPU memory fragmentation and 50% memory retained across crashes -> node becomes unhealthy, cordoned by autoscaler -> cluster reports node flaps and pods landing on gpu-13 which then also hit OOM.

carol (prodeng): customer impact: we saw ~4% 5xx for text-generation for a short window. enterprise-corp-X and startup-beta saw elevated latency/errors. I'm collecting request ids for support.

dave (ml infra): model-10-big warmup path loads full fp32 weights by default; warmup-deserialization is single-threaded and spikes memory. suspects: new quantization metadata in version v3 that changed deserialization memory pattern.

ben (sre): mitigation plan (live): 1) stop further rollouts of model-10-big, 2) take impacted nodes out of rotation (cordon/drain), 3) pin runtime route to model-10-quantized-v2 fallback, 4) disable automatic warmup for large models temporarily.

alice (oncall): executing now. running: 
```bash
# cordon node with flaps
kubectl cordon gpu-12
kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
# scale down replica set for model-10-big
kubectl scale --replicas=0 rs/model-10-big-loader
# flip feature flag to use quantized fallback
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://controlplane/api/routes/pin?route=text-gen&model=model-10-quantized-v2"
# disable warmup env var for group
kubectl set env deployment/serving-runtime RUNTIME_MODEL_WARMUP=false
```

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook check: Warmup disable is an approved mitigation for load-time OOMs. Watch for increased first-request latency. Notify customers if 5xx > 1% for 10m.

ben (sre): verifying GPU state: ran `nvidia-smi -i 0 -q -d MEMORY` on gpu-12 before drain; memory was ~28 GiB allocated persistent fragments. recommend full node reboot if it doesn't recover after drain.

alice (oncall): pinned route success, traffic shifted to quantized fallback. scaling of model-10-big stopped. warmup disabled cluster-wide for service. restarting the failing pod with smaller LD_PRELOAD chunk size and TORCH_USE_CUDA_DYNAMYCACHE=0 as a test.

dave (ml infra): quick patch: new loader will stream-deserialize tensors (decompress in chunks) but not deployed yet. can we keep fallback live while we roll patch?

carol (prodeng): notifying affected customers: support posts drafted for enterprise-corp-X and startup-beta. message: "We've detected transient model load failures affecting a subset of requests; we've routed you to a fallback quantized model to maintain availability while we investigate."

ben (sre): after mitigation, error rate down from 4% to 0.3% within 7 minutes. latency bump +200ms p50 on fallback. No new node flaps seen in 15m.

alice (oncall): performing handoff to ben for follow-up and root cause. ben, you're oncall for next hour.

ben (sre): taking over. current actions: 1) schedule node reboot for gpu-12 and gpu-13 if they show memory leak post-restart, 2) coordinate with dave to roll the streaming-deserialize patch to canary, 3) produce incident summary and customer impact for CS.

alice (oncall): leaving notes: timeline, commands run, logs attached to thread. escalation: if error rate >1% again, escalate to infra-leads + paging.

dave (ml infra): canary deploy plan: build loader v1.2.3-stream, deploy to canary namespace with `MODEL_WARMUP=false` and `STREAM_DESERIALIZE=1`, target 2 non-prod nodes for now. health checks focused on `model_load_time` and `cuda_alloc_failures`.

carol (prodeng): CS update: customers notified, commercial impact assessed as low for now but enterprise-corp-X is logging a support ticket.

ben (sre): post-mitigation checks: run `kubectl get pods -o wide` to confirm no CrashLoopBackOffs, run `kubectl top pods` to check memory/CPU, and `journalctl -u kubelet` on nodes for OOMKill spikes.

sre-runbook-bot: Suggested postmortem template: Summary, impact, timeline, root cause hypotheses, mitigation steps, long-term fixes (loader patch, warmup gating, canary policy), owners, MWT.

ben (sre): assigning follow-ups: dave -> loader patch + canary (ETA 4h), alice -> node reboots + infra ticket (ETA 1h), carol -> customer comms + support bundle (ETA 30m), ben -> write incident summary and schedule postmortem (ETA 2h).

alice (oncall): leaving thread. good recovery.

ben (sre): closing note: incident marked resolved at 1765502850. We'll keep the fallback pinned until loader patch is validated. Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 14:00 PST.
